prompt: Using only a reviewer-owned sanitized cost, usage, observability and product-outcome packet—or an explicitly isolated non-production billing sandbox—diagnose and resolve an unfamiliar cost-and-value incident. The reviewer secretly injects one data-semantics defect, one ownership or allocation defect, one forecast or budget defect, one anomaly or security defect, one optimization or commitment defect and one outcome-reconciliation or communication defect. Work without model-answer material and make no production or purchasing decision.
deliverables: Named decision, owner, scope, currency, periods, expected value, risk appetite and refusal conditions
Source inventory covering provider or generator, export, schema, query, load, completeness, corrections and invoice boundary
Cost semantic table for list, contracted, billed, effective, adjustment and invoice measures used
Account, project, subscription, resource, product, service, environment, team and cost-center ownership map
Direct, shared, idle, platform, support and adjustment pool analysis with allocation coverage
Versioned shared-cost driver, weights, rounding and source-to-target conservation proof
Stable fully loaded unit-cost calculation tied to an engineering and business outcome
Estimate, forecast, uncertainty range, backtest, budget, actual and variance comparison
Dimensional cost-anomaly timeline separating data, quantity, rate, allocation, architecture, waste and abuse hypotheses
Sanitized audit/security correlation and accountable incident routing
Optimization options with utilization, SLO, error-budget, performance, capacity and largest-failure reserve evidence
Commitment portfolio analysis covering eligible baseline, coverage, utilization, vacancy, flexibility, concentration, term and break-even
Approved disposable canary plan with blast radius, stop thresholds, rollback and user validation
Realized-savings or cost-avoidance reconciliation plan with implementation cost and demand normalization
Executive and engineering narratives stating assumptions, uncertainty, alternatives, residual risk, owner and next review
Exact temporary access, query, export, file, dashboard, alert, resource and exception cleanup evidence
evidenceRequirements: Use no production mutation, unrestricted cloud credential, customer data, confidential contract values in Git or current purchase authority
Reviewer owns sanitization, hidden defects, sandbox scope, query-cost ceiling, action authority, scoring and cleanup
Bind the exact dataset and transformation version before making any numerical claim
Use one currency and aligned periods or document conversion source, timestamp and sensitivity
Do not mix list, contracted, billed, effective or invoice cost without an explicit reconciliation
Measure missing, late, duplicated, corrected and unallocated data and preserve uncertainty
Every allocated source amount must be directly owned, intentionally retained or distributed by a declared rule, and totals must conserve
Unit denominators must be versioned, stable, measurable and resistant to retries, failure and gaming
Separate estimate, forecast, budget, actual, anomaly and invoice with distinct owners and timestamps
Treat cost anomalies as possible security, reliability, demand, rate, data or allocation incidents until evidence separates them
No rightsizing, shutdown, deletion, topology or architecture proposal may cross SLO, failure-reserve, durability, security or recovery gates
No commitment recommendation may rely on an anomalous interval or omit flexibility, vacancy, concentration and term scenarios
Every proposed mutation requires separate authorization, a bounded canary, stop conditions, rollback and representative user proof
Estimated opportunity, cost avoidance and realized saving must remain separate and include implementation cost
Reviewer independently verifies sensitive-data handling and exact cleanup

Maps hierarchy pools coverage driver fairness and exact conservation

Separates states models demand seasonality rates uncertainty backtest and owners
Decomposes drivers checks abuse preserves evidence and routes response

States assumptions uncertainty residual risk owners cadence and proves exact cleanup
